sanskrit: dharmavyucchittim icchanto ye 'dharmasya pravartakāḥ hantavyās te durātmāno devair daityā ivolbaṇāḥ
english: Those evil-souled men who, seeking the destruction of dharma, become the promoters of adharma, must be slain—even as the fierce Daityas were slain by the gods.

sanskrit: ekaṃ hatvā yadi kule śiṣṭānāṃ syād anāmayam kulaṃ hatvātha rāṣṭraṃ vā na tad vṛttopaghātakam
english: If by killing one man the welfare of the rest of a family is secured, or by destroying a family or even a kingdom, then such an act does no injury to right conduct.

sanskrit: adharmarūpo dharmo hi kaś cid asti narādhipa dharmaś cādharmarūpo 'sti tac ca jñeyaṃ vipaścitā
english: For there is, O lord of men, a dharma that wears the form of adharma, and an adharma that wears the form of dharma; this the wise man must learn to discern.

sanskrit: tasmāt saṃstambhayātmānaṃ śrutavān asi pāṇḍava devaiḥ pūrvagataṃ mārgam anuyāto 'si bhārata
english: Therefore steady your heart, O Pāṇḍava, for you are learned; you have followed the path trodden of old by the gods themselves, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: na hīdṛśā gamiṣyanti narakaṃ pāṇḍavarṣabha bhrātṝn āśvāsayaitāṃs tvaṃ suhṛdaś ca paraṃtapa
english: Men such as you do not go to hell, O bull of the Pāṇḍavas; comfort these your brothers and your friends, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: yo hi pāpasamārambhe kārye tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ kurvann api tathaiva syāt kṛtvā ca nirapatrapaḥ
english: For he who, set upon a sinful undertaking, is wholly possessed by that intent—who acts in that same spirit while doing it, and remains shameless once it is done—

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tat kaluṣaṃ sarvaṃ samāptam iti śabditam prāyaścittaṃ na tasyāsti hrāso vā pāpakarmaṇaḥ
english: in him, it is said, all that taint reaches its fullness: for such a one there is no expiation, nor any lessening of the evil deed.

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu śuklābhijātīyaḥ paradoṣeṇa kāritaḥ anicchamānaḥ karmedaṃ kṛtvā ca paritapyase
english: But you are of pure birth, made to act by another's fault; unwillingly you wrought this deed, and now you grieve for having done it.

sanskrit: aśvamedho mahāyajñaḥ prāyaścittam udāhṛtam tam āhara mahārāja vipāpmaivaṃ bhaviṣyasi
english: The horse-sacrifice, the great offering, is declared to be the expiation; perform it, O great king, and thus you shall be cleansed of evil.

sanskrit: marudbhiḥ saha jitvārīn maghavān pākaśāsanaḥ ekaikaṃ kratum āhṛtya śatakṛtvaḥ śatakratuḥ
english: Maghavat, the chastiser of Pāka, having vanquished his foes together with the Maruts, by performing one sacrifice after another a hundredfold, became the Lord of a Hundred Sacrifices.

sanskrit: pūtapāpmā jitasvargo lokān prāpya sukhodayān marudgaṇavṛtaḥ śakraḥ śuśubhe bhāsayan diśaḥ
english: Cleansed of sin, having won heaven and attained the worlds where bliss arises, Śakra, surrounded by the host of the Maruts, shone resplendent, lighting up the quarters.

sanskrit: svargaloke mahīyantam apsarobhiḥ śacīpatim ṛṣayaḥ paryupāsante devāś ca vibudheśvaram
english: As the lord of Śacī is honored in the world of heaven amid the Apsarases, the sages wait upon him, and the gods too attend that ruler of the wise.

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ tvam iha saṃkrānto vikrameṇa vasuṃdharām nirjitāś ca mahīpālā vikrameṇa tvayānagha
english: Even such are you, who here by your valor have passed over the whole earth, and by your valor have conquered its guardian-kings, O sinless one.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ purāṇi rāṣṭrāṇi gatvā rājan suhṛdvṛtaḥ bhrātṝn putrāṃś ca pautrāṃś ca sve sve rājye 'bhiṣecaya
english: Go to their cities and kingdoms, O king, surrounded by your friends, and consecrate their brothers, sons, and grandsons each in his own realm.

sanskrit: bālān api ca garbhasthān sāntvāni samudācaran rañjayan prakṛtīḥ sarvāḥ paripāhi vasuṃdharām
english: Even the children, even those still in the womb—speaking words of comfort, gladdening all your subjects, do you protect the earth.

sanskrit: kumāro nāsti yeṣāṃ ca kanyās tatrābhiṣecaya kāmāśayo hi strīvargaḥ śokam evaṃ prahāsyati
english: And where there is no son, there consecrate the daughters; for womankind is set upon desire, and thus they will lay aside their grief.

sanskrit: evam āśvāsanaṃ kṛtvā sarvarāṣṭreṣu bhārata yajasva vājimedhena yathendro vijayī purā
english: When you have thus brought solace to all the kingdoms, O Bhārata, offer the horse-sacrifice, as Indra the victorious did of old.

sanskrit: aśocyās te mahātmānaḥ kṣatriyāḥ kṣatriyarṣabha svakarmabhir gatā nāśaṃ kṛtāntabalamohitāḥ
english: Those great-souled warriors are not to be mourned, O bull among Kṣatriyas; by their own deeds they met their ruin, bewildered by the power of fate.

sanskrit: avāptaḥ kṣatradharmas te rājyaṃ prāptam akalmaṣam carasva dharmaṃ kaunteya śreyān yaḥ pretya bhāvikaḥ
english: The duty of a Kṣatriya you have fulfilled, and your kingdom is won unstained; walk now in that dharma, O son of Kuntī, which yields the higher good in the life beyond.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kāni kṛtveha karmāṇi prāyaścittīyate naraḥ kiṃ kṛtvā caiva mucyeta tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: By doing what deeds in this world does a man come to need expiation, and by doing what is he set free? Tell me that, O grandsire.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca akurvan vihitaṃ karma pratiṣiddhāni cācaran prāyaścittīyate hy evaṃ naro mithyā ca vartayan
english: Vyāsa said: By leaving undone the ordained acts, by performing the forbidden ones, and by living falsely—thus does a man come to need expiation.

sanskrit: sūryeṇābhyudito yaś ca brahmacārī bhavaty uta tathā sūryābhinirmuktaḥ kunakhī śyāvadann api
english: The student of the Veda upon whom the sun rises while he still sleeps, or upon whom it sets, the man with diseased nails, the man with discolored teeth—

sanskrit: parivittiḥ parivettā brahmojjho yaś ca kutsakaḥ didhiṣūpatis tathā yaḥ syād agredidhiṣur eva ca
english: the man married before his elder brother and the man whose younger brother weds before him, the forsaker of the Veda and the reviler of it, the husband of a remarried woman, and the man who weds before his elder brother—

sanskrit: avakīrṇī bhaved yaś ca dvijātivadhakas tathā atīrthe brahmaṇas tyāgī tīrthe cāpratipādakaḥ
english: he who has broken his vow of chastity, the slayer of a twice-born man, he who abandons sacred learning to an unworthy recipient and he who withholds it from a worthy one—

sanskrit: grāmayājī ca kaunteya rājñaś ca parivikrayī śūdrastrīvadhako yaś ca pūrvaḥ pūrvas tu garhitaḥ
english: the village-priest, O son of Kuntī, the seller of a king's secrets, and the slayer of a Śūdra woman—of these, each earlier-named is the more to be condemned.

sanskrit: vṛthāpaśusamālambhī vanadāhasya kārakaḥ anṛtenopacartā ca pratiroddhā guros tathā
english: He who slaughters an animal in vain, he who sets fire to a forest, he who serves another with falsehood, and he who opposes his teacher—

sanskrit: yaś cāgnīn apavidhyeta tathaiva brahmavikrayī etāny enāṃsi sarvāṇi vyutkrāntasamayaś ca yaḥ
english: and he who casts away his sacred fires, and likewise the seller of the Veda, and he who has broken his sworn agreement—all these are counted among the sins.

sanskrit: akāryāṇy api vakṣyāmi yāni tāni nibodha me lokavedaviruddhāni tāny ekāgramanāḥ śṛṇu
english: I shall also tell of the things that ought not to be done; learn them from me—deeds opposed to the world and the Veda; hear them with single-minded attention.

sanskrit: svadharmasya parityāgaḥ paradharmasya ca kriyā ayājyayājanaṃ caiva tathābhakṣyasya bhakṣaṇam
english: The abandonment of one's own duty and the practice of another's; the officiating at sacrifices for those unfit to sacrifice; and the eating of what ought not to be eaten;

sanskrit: śaraṇāgatasaṃtyāgo bhṛtyasyābharaṇaṃ tathā rasānāṃ vikrayaś cāpi tiryagyonivadhas tathā
english: the forsaking of one who has come for refuge, the failure to support a dependent, the selling of flavored liquids, and the slaying of beasts of the brute-born kind;

sanskrit: ādhānādīni karmāṇi śaktimān na karoti yaḥ aprayacchaṃś ca sarvāṇi nityaṃ deyāni bhārata
english: the failure of a capable man to perform the kindling of the fires and the like, and the withholding of all those things, O Bhārata, that ought ever to be given—

sanskrit: dakṣiṇānām adānaṃ ca brāhmaṇasvābhimarśanam sarvāṇy etāny akāryāṇi prāhur dharmavido janāḥ
english: the failure to bestow sacrificial fees, and the laying of hands upon a Brāhmaṇa's property—all these the knowers of dharma declare to be deeds not to be done.

sanskrit: pitrā vibhajate putro yaś ca syād gurutalpagaḥ aprajāyann adharmeṇa bhavaty ādharmiko janaḥ
english: The son who divides the inheritance against his father's will, he who defiles his teacher's bed, and he who fails to beget offspring—through such unrighteousness a man becomes a doer of adharma.

sanskrit: uktāny etāni karmāṇi vistareṇetareṇa ca yāni kurvann akurvaṃś ca prāyaścittīyate janaḥ
english: These deeds have now been told, both at length and in brief—the deeds by doing or by failing to do which a man comes to need expiation.

sanskrit: etāny eva tu karmāṇi kriyamāṇāni mānavān yeṣu yeṣu nimitteṣu na limpanty atha tac chṛṇu
english: But hear now under what particular circumstances these very same deeds, when performed, do not stain men with guilt.

sanskrit: pragṛhya śastram āyāntam api vedāntagaṃ raṇe jighāṃsantaṃ nihatyājau na tena brahmahā bhavet
english: If a man slays in battle even one versed in the end of the Veda who comes against him with weapon raised, intent on killing, he does not by that become a slayer of a Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: api cāpy atra kaunteya mantro vedeṣu paṭhyate vedapramāṇavihitaṃ taṃ dharmaṃ prabravīmi te
english: And moreover, O son of Kuntī, a sacred verse upon this is recited in the Vedas; I declare to you that dharma as ordained by the authority of the Veda.

sanskrit: apetaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vṛttād yo hanyād ātatāyinam na tena brahmahā sa syān manyus taṃ manyum ṛcchati
english: He who slays a Brāhmaṇa fallen from his rightful conduct, an aggressor with weapon poised, does not thereby become a slayer of a Brāhmaṇa; it is one wrath answering another.

sanskrit: prāṇātyaye tathājñānād ācaran madirām api acodito dharmaparaḥ punaḥ saṃskāram arhati
english: In peril of life, or through ignorance, even one devoted to dharma who drinks strong liquor—if unprompted to it—deserves once more to be purified by the sacraments.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ kaunteyābhakṣyabhakṣaṇam prāyaścittavidhānena sarvam etena śudhyati
english: All this concerning the eating of what should not be eaten has been told to you, O son of Kuntī; through the ordinance of expiation all of it is purified.

sanskrit: gurutalpaṃ hi gurvarthe na dūṣayati mānavam uddālakaḥ śvetaketuṃ janayām āsa śiṣyataḥ
english: For the approaching of the teacher's bed, when done at the teacher's bidding, does not defile a man: Uddālaka begot Śvetaketu through a pupil in just this way.

sanskrit: steyaṃ kurvaṃs tu gurvartham āpatsu na nibadhyate bahuśaḥ kāmakāreṇa na ced yaḥ saṃpravartate
english: He who commits theft for his teacher's sake in times of distress is not bound by it, provided he does not turn to it again and again out of wilful desire.

sanskrit: anyatra brāhmaṇasvebhya ādadāno na duṣyati svayam aprāśitā yaś ca na sa pāpena lipyate
english: He who takes such property, save that of a Brāhmaṇa, incurs no fault; and he who does not himself partake of it is not tainted by sin.

sanskrit: prāṇatrāṇe 'nṛtaṃ vācyam ātmano vā parasya vā gurvarthe strīṣu caiva syād vivāhakaraṇeṣu ca
english: A falsehood may be spoken to save life, one's own or another's; and so too for the teacher's sake, in matters concerning women, and in the making of marriages.

sanskrit: nāvartate vrataṃ svapne śukramokṣe kathaṃ cana ājyahomaḥ samiddhe 'gnau prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate
english: A vow is not broken by an emission of seed in a dream by any means; an oblation of clarified butter upon the kindled fire is ordained as the expiation.

sanskrit: pārivittyaṃ ca patite nāsti pravrajite tathā bhikṣite pāradāryaṃ ca na tad dharmasya dūṣakam
english: There is no offense of marrying before an elder brother who has become an outcaste, or who has gone forth as an ascetic or a mendicant; and the taking of his wife in such a case is no violation of dharma.

sanskrit: vṛthāpaśusamālambhaṃ naiva kuryān na kārayet anugrahaḥ paśūṇāṃ hi saṃskāro vidhicoditaḥ
english: One should neither slaughter an animal in vain nor cause it to be done; for the sacramental slaying of beasts, when ordained by the rule, is in truth a grace bestowed upon them.

sanskrit: anarhe brāhmaṇe dattam ajñānāt tan na dūṣakam sakāraṇaṃ tathā tīrthe 'tīrthe vā pratipādanam
english: What is given to an unworthy Brāhmaṇa through ignorance is no offense; and so too the imparting of learning, for due cause, whether to a worthy or an unworthy recipient.

sanskrit: striyas tathāpacāriṇyo niṣkṛtiḥ syād adūṣikā api sā pūyate tena na tu bhartā praduṣyate
english: For women who have transgressed there is an atonement free of blame; by it even she is purified, and the husband is not thereby defiled.

sanskrit: tattvaṃ jñātvā tu somasya vikrayaḥ syād adūṣakaḥ asamarthasya bhṛtyasya visargaḥ syād adoṣavān vanadāho gavām arthe kriyamāṇo na dūṣakaḥ
english: Knowing its true nature, the sale of Soma may be made without fault; the dismissal of a dependent who is incapable is without offense; and the burning of a forest, when done for the sake of cattle, is no transgression.

sanskrit: uktāny etāni karmāṇi yāni kurvan na duṣyati prāyaścittāni vakṣyāmi vistareṇaiva bhārata
english: These deeds have been told, by doing which a man incurs no fault; now I shall declare the expiations at length, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca tapasā karmabhiś caiva pradānena ca bhārata punāti pāpaṃ puruṣaḥ pūtaś cen na pravartate
english: Vyāsa said: By austerity, by rites, and by gifts, O Bhārata, a man cleanses away his sin—if, once purified, he does not return to it again.

sanskrit: ekakālaṃ tu bhuñjānaś caran bhaikṣaṃ svakarmakṛt kapālapāṇiḥ khaṭvāṅgī brahmacārī sadotthitaḥ
english: Eating but once a day, wandering for alms, performing his own observance, a skull in his hand and a club at his side, chaste, ever alert,

sanskrit: anasūyur adhaḥśāyī karma loke prakāśayan pūrṇair dvādaśabhir varṣair brahmahā vipramucyate
english: free of malice, sleeping upon the ground, proclaiming his deed before the world—after twelve full years the slayer of a Brāhmaṇa is set free.

sanskrit: ṣaḍbhir varṣaiḥ kṛcchrabhojī brahmahā pūyate naraḥ māse māse samaśnaṃs tu tribhir varṣaiḥ pramucyate
english: In six years a man who lives on penitential fare is cleansed of the slaying of a Brāhmaṇa; eating but once each month, he is freed in three years.

sanskrit: saṃvatsareṇa māsāśī pūyate nātra saṃśayaḥ tathaivoparaman rājan svalpenāpi pramucyate
english: He who eats but once a month is purified within a single year, of this there is no doubt; and likewise, O king, one who abstains from food is freed even by a lesser term.

sanskrit: kratunā cāśvamedhena pūyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ya cāsyāvabhṛthe snānti ke cid evaṃvidhā narāḥ
english: By the rite of the horse-sacrifice he is purified, of this there is no doubt; and whatever men bathe at its concluding ablution—

sanskrit: te sarve pūtapāpmāno bhavantīti parā śrutiḥ brāhmaṇārthe hato yuddhe mucyate brahmahatyayā
english: all of them become cleansed of sin, so runs the highest sacred tradition; and he who is slain in battle for a Brāhmaṇa's sake is freed from the guilt of Brāhmaṇa-slaying.

sanskrit: gavāṃ śatasahasraṃ tu pātrebhyaḥ pratipādayan brahmahā vipramucyeta sarvapāpebhya eva ca
english: By bestowing a hundred thousand cows upon worthy recipients, the slayer of a Brāhmaṇa is set free from that and from all sins as well.

sanskrit: kapilānāṃ sahasrāṇi yo dadyāt pañcaviṃśatim dogdhrīṇāṃ sa ca pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyo vipramucyate
english: He who gives twenty-five thousand tawny milch-cows is freed from all his sins.

sanskrit: gosahasraṃ savatsānāṃ dogdhrīṇāṃ prāṇasaṃśaye sādhubhyo vai daridrebhyo dattvā mucyeta kilbiṣāt
english: In peril of life, by giving a thousand milch-cows with their calves to the virtuous who are poor, a man is freed from his guilt.

sanskrit: śataṃ tai yas tu kāmbojān brāhmaṇebhyaḥ prayacchati niyatebhyo mahīpāla sa ca pāpāt pramucyate
english: He who gives a hundred Kāmboja horses to Brāhmaṇas of disciplined life, O guardian of the earth, he too is released from his sin.

sanskrit: manorathaṃ tu yo dadyād ekasmā api bhārata na kīrtayeta dattvā yaḥ sa ca pāpāt pramucyate
english: He who fulfills the heart's desire of even a single man, O Bhārata, and who, having given, does not proclaim it abroad—he too is released from his sin.

sanskrit: surāpānaṃ sakṛt pītvā yo 'gnivarṇāṃ pibed dvijaḥ sa pāvayaty athātmānam iha loke paratra ca
english: A twice-born man who, having once drunk strong liquor, then drinks it fire-hot, thereby purifies himself both in this world and the next.

sanskrit: meruprapātaṃ prapatañ jvalanaṃ vā samāviśan mahāprasthānam ātiṣṭhan mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ
english: By casting himself from the heights of Meru, or by entering the fire, or by setting forth upon the Great Journey, he is freed from all his sins.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatisaveneṣṭvā surāpo brāhmaṇaḥ punaḥ samitiṃ brāhmaṇair gacched iti vai brāhmaṇī śrutiḥ
english: A Brāhmaṇa who has drunk liquor, having sacrificed with the Bṛhaspati-sava rite, may once more join the assembly of Brāhmaṇas—so runs the sacred tradition of the Brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: bhūmipradānaṃ kuryād yaḥ surāṃ pītvā vimatsaraḥ punar na ca pibed rājan saṃskṛtaḥ śudhyate naraḥ
english: He who, having drunk liquor, makes a gift of land without grudging and drinks no more, O king—that man, once sanctified by the sacraments, is purified.

sanskrit: gurutalpī śilāṃ taptām āyasīm adhisaṃviśet pāṇāv ādhāya vā śephaṃ pravrajed ūrdhvadarśanaḥ
english: He who has defiled his teacher's bed should lie down upon a heated slab of iron, or, taking his own member in his hand, should go forth gazing upward.

sanskrit: śarīrasya vimokṣeṇa mucyate karmaṇo 'śubhāt karmabhyo vipramucyante yattāḥ saṃvatsaraṃ striyaḥ
english: By the surrender of the body he is freed from the evil deed; and women who keep restraint for a year are released from such deeds.

sanskrit: mahāvrataṃ cared yas tu dadyāt sarvasvam eva tu gurvarthe vā hato yuddhe sa mucyet karmaṇo 'śubhāt
english: He who performs the Great Vow, or gives away all that he possesses, or is slain in battle for his teacher's sake, is released from the evil deed.

sanskrit: anṛtenopacartā ca pratiroddhā guros tathā upahṛtya priyaṃ tasmai tasmāt pāpāt pramucyate
english: He who has served another with falsehood, and he who has opposed his teacher, by rendering to him what is dear, are released from that sin.

sanskrit: avakīrṇinimittaṃ tu brahmahatyāvrataṃ caret kharacarmavāsāḥ ṣaṇmāsaṃ tathā mucyeta kilbiṣāt
english: For the breaking of the vow of chastity, one should observe the penance prescribed for the slaying of a Brāhmaṇa, clad in an ass's hide for six months; thus is he freed from his guilt.

sanskrit: paradārāpahārī ca parasyāpaharan vasu saṃvatsaraṃ vratī bhūtvā tathā mucyeta kilbiṣāt
english: He who has carried off another's wife, and he who has seized another's wealth, by holding a vow for a full year, are thus freed from their guilt.

sanskrit: steyaṃ tu yasyāpaharet tasmai dadyāt samaṃ vasu vividhenābhyupāyena tena mucyeta kilbiṣāt
english: From whomever one has stolen, to him one should give back wealth of equal worth; by such manifold means is one freed from that guilt.

sanskrit: kṛcchrād dvādaśarātreṇa svabhyastena daśāvaram parivettā bhavet pūtaḥ parivittiś ca bhārata
english: By a penance of twelve nights well observed, or of no fewer than ten, both he who married before his elder brother and the elder brother so passed over are made pure, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: niveśyaṃ tu bhavet tena sadā tārayitā pitṝn na tu striyā bhaved doṣo na tu sā tena lipyate
english: He should then take a wife, ever delivering his forefathers thereby; and upon the woman no fault falls, nor is she tainted by it.

sanskrit: bhajane hy ṛtunā śuddhaṃ cāturmāsyaṃ vidhīyate striyas tena viśudhyanti iti dharmavido viduḥ
english: For in conjugal union, purified by the season, a four-month observance is ordained; by it women are made pure, so the knowers of dharma understand.

sanskrit: striyas tv āśaṅkitāḥ pāpair nopagamyā hi jānatā rajasā tā viśudhyante bhasmanā bhājanaṃ yathā
english: But women suspected of sins are not to be approached by a man who knows; by their monthly courses they are made pure, as a vessel is cleansed by ashes.

sanskrit: catuṣpāt sakalo dharmo brāhmaṇānāṃ vidhīyate pādāvakṛṣṭo rājanye tathā dharmo vidhīyate
english: For Brāhmaṇas the whole of dharma is ordained, complete on all four feet; for the Kṣatriya the dharma is ordained drawn short by one foot.

sanskrit: tathā vaiśye ca śūdre ca pādaḥ pādo vidhīyate vidyād evaṃvidhenaiṣāṃ gurulāghavaniścayam
english: So too for the Vaiśya and the Śūdra, foot by foot it is diminished; by this measure one should determine the greater and lesser weight of their duties.
